response.rationale: Bone marrow infiltration with 24.6% abnormal cells plus B-cell-associated markers and widespread PET/CT lymphomatous disease support lymphoma in leukemic phase; hypercalcemia with suppressed PTH and high LDH are typical complications. DLBCL is not clearly supported by CD20(-)/CD5(3+), and sepsis, lactic acidosis, and hypercalcemia are secondary features.

rejected.why: Fever and leukocytosis are nonspecific and can be caused by aggressive lymphoma; no infection source is documented and it does not explain hypercalcemia or marrow involvement.
Lymphoma is close but omits the leukemic-phase qualifier supported by 24.6% marrow abnormal cells.
CD20(-) and CD5(3+) are not supportive of DLBCL, and no DLBCL-defining markers are provided.
Lactic acidosis is a metabolic complication of the underlying malignancy, not the primary diagnosis.
Hypercalcemia with low PTH is a paraneoplastic syndrome caused by the lymphoma, not the most likely overall diagnosis.
